issue: The FIND-004 remediation double-counts the egress walk when computing door-to-door durationSecs. parseTransitPlan does `durationSecs: (best.durationSecs || 0) + walk` where `walk = accessWalkSecs + egressWalkSecs`. But the committed fixture proves `best.durationSecs` (the raw transit.ls8h.com journey-level field) ALREADY includes the egress walk: for journey[0], leg.arrivalSecs=84180 (train arrival) while journey.arrivalSecs=84309 — the 129s difference IS egressWalkSecs, and journey.departureSecs(83280)==leg.departureSecs(83280) (train-departure time, i.e. NOT reduced by accessWalkSecs). So best.durationSecs=1029 already = in-vehicle(900)+egress(129). Adding accessWalkSecs+egressWalkSecs again yields 1029+61+129=1219 — egress is counted TWICE (once embedded in the raw field, once added). The mathematically correct door-to-door value is best.durationSecs + accessWalkSecs = 1029+61=1090, not 1219. This pattern holds identically across all 3 transit journeys in the fixture (journey[1]: 969=840+129 egress-embedded; journey[2]: 969=840+129 egress-embedded), so it is not a fixture fluke. The bug is now baked into the unit test itself (transit.test.js:29 asserts durationSecs===1219), so the test enforces the wrong formula and gives false confidence that FIND-004 is fixed. The `inVehicleSecs: best.durationSecs` field (transit.js:48) is also mislabeled — it is actually in-vehicle+egress, not pure in-vehicle time.
evidence: .vcsdd/features/life-manager-cost-connect-reliability/evidence/fixtures/transit-plan-tokyo-shinjuku.json journey[0]: departureSecs=83280 (== leg.departureSecs=83280, no access-walk offset applied to the journey-level departure), arrivalSecs=84309, leg.arrivalSecs=84180 → 84309-84180=129==egressWalkSecs (embedded in the raw durationSecs=1029=900+129). apps/life-call/lib/transit.js:45-47: `const walk = (Number(best.accessWalkSecs)||0)+(Number(best.egressWalkSecs)||0); return { durationSecs: (best.durationSecs||0)+walk, ... }` re-adds egressWalkSecs a second time. apps/life-call/lib/transit.test.js:29 `assert.equal(r.durationSecs, 1219)` codifies the over-count as 'correct'.
fix: Change parseTransitPlan to `durationSecs: (best.durationSecs || 0) + (Number(best.accessWalkSecs) || 0)` (do NOT re-add egressWalkSecs, it is already inside best.durationSecs per this API's observed contract). Recompute the fixture-derived expected value (1090, not 1219) and update transit.test.js accordingly. Note: the direction of the current bug is conservative (over-estimate, not under-estimate), so it does not violate the never-late invariant, but it is still an unproven, evidence-contradicted arithmetic claim shipped as 'FIXED + verified' in execution-notes.md.
